lastCredNameFilter.note: STRUCTURAL FIX. Nine tools select credentials from .env BY NAME using a regex requiring KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD - which GITHUB_PAT matches NONE of, so a live push-capable PAT was invisible to every scanner and redactor. Nine identical copies of the same filter, so fixing one would have changed nothing. Now ONE definition in ops/cred_name_filter.py, imported by all of them. The PAT rule is a whole underscore-delimited SEGMENT: GITHUB_PAT/GH_PAT match; PATH, GITHUB_PATH, COMPAT, PATCH, PATTERN do NOT - a plain substring would have matched PATH and turned every PATH-shaped variable into a credential, drowning the real findings. A rule that fires on correct code teaches people to ignore it. ALSO: ops/tmp-credential-surface-audit.py carried a SECOND copy of the liveness probe table and the scanner imports it, so the classifier fix in the redactor changed nothing for the scanner - it now delegates to the shared classifier. Two copies of a classifier always drift, and the more aggressive one wins by accident.

lastDiscordPost.content: Root cause: blotato-fallback.js declared its targets with a hardcoded media: [] and post() sends mediaUrls: target.media verbatim, so every fallback publish shipped with no picture; the pending file DOES carry the image (media.image = public CDN URL) and the fallback never read it. Only Threads because LinkedIn's grant is dead and Threads is the one platform that works - the live data agrees, every imageless post is a Threads post. Fixed at source: the image is resolved from the pending file and attached, but ONLY if the URL is still live (probed first; a dead image falls back to the old behaviour so a broken image cannot turn a working publish into a failing one); the 22 Oct image URL is still live. CORRECTION of my 04:02 message: the content agent does NOT publish at 08:55 - it tries Facebook, the token 190s as expected, and QUEUES the caption; the fallback publishes it; and the fallback record is empty for 23-27 Oct, so path B has not shipped a caption since 22 Oct. Decision (a) is therefore moot for path B - it now publishes WITH the image. The one residual is path A: the pillar publisher still ships imageless if the queue file has no Media URL (the 08:00 gate alarms, does not block); tonight's queue file has one (200 image/png) so tonight's 09:00 post carries its picture. Whether that residual becomes a hard refusal is still Tumelo's call. Test: 14 assertions, fails against the pre-fix source. Suite: 48 python + 5 other, all pass.

lessons.a_404_is_inconclusive_not_dead: GitHub's REST API lives at api.github.com. Probing github.com/api/... returns HTTP 404, which is INCONCLUSIVE, not proof of death. My first probe of the tracked .netrc hit exactly this and I had to correct it. Same discipline as the 401/403 rule, one status code over: never read a 404 as 'the key is dead'.
lessons.a_check_that_cannot_fail_is_worse_than_n: 2026-10-23: my new rule 4b first flagged the note's quoted historical figure, then read the row-number column, then the Company column, instead of the email count. All three bugs were invisible without negative-tests WITH A CONTROL CASE. A rule that false-positives on correct code teaches people to ignore the whole checker.
lessons.a_checker_that_cannot_reach_the_live_pag: 2026-10-23: a React SPA returns ~150 chars of HTML shell, so text assertions against the fetched page proved nothing - 4 live pages had ZERO assertions and two of them published 'Rainforest Alliance certified' and 'certified Russian caviar houses' while the checker said UNCHECKED. Assert the BUILT BUNDLE, and prove the live site serves that build: a fixed source with no redeploy is STALE BUILD, not a pass.
lessons.a_checker_that_validates_a_path_nothing_: 2026-10-27 16:40 UTC: the repo sets core.hooksPath=.githooks, so git runs .githooks/pre-push and NEVER LOOKS AT .git/hooks/. My guard was installed to .git/hooks/ and my checker validated .git/hooks/ - they agreed with each other, both reported CLEAN, and the guard had NEVER EXECUTED ONCE. A checker that validates a path nothing reads is a checker that always passes: it is worse than no checker, because it manufactures false confidence about a control that is not running. Two files agreeing proved nothing - they agreed because one was a copy of the other and NEITHER was reachable. Fix: resolve the hooks dir the way git does (git config --get core.hooksPath, relative to repo root, else .git/hooks), check the guard THERE, and print the resolved path. Corollary: a checker needs NEGATIVE CONTROLS, and to have them it must be testable against something other than the one healthy repo it was written for - hence GUARD_CHECK_REPO. The first version hard-coded /workspace and the negative controls failed; the test was right, the checker was untestable. And 'installed' is not 'running' - prove it with a real push (to a local bare repo, never the public one).
lessons.a_checker_written_to_catch_a_nasty_failu: 2026-10-27: ops/check-git-index.py exists to catch an emptied index. It is only meaningful if it CAN fail, so ops/test-git-index-check.py drives it against scratch repos damaged four ways: emptied index, missing index, index disagreeing with HEAD, and a healthy repo. A checker with no negative control is decoration. Same pattern as the pre-push guard checker, which also needed GUARD_CHECK_REPO to be testable at all.
lessons.a_checkers_parser_is_part_of_the_check: 2026-10-23: the credential checker reported CLEAN while 16 LIVE keys sat in tracked markdown in the PUBLIC remote. Tightening the ALLOW regex did not close the hole - prose_line_numbers() treats every .md line as prose and the HARDCODED check SKIPS prose, so a SECOND mechanism re-opened the blind spot the fix had just closed. The evidence was not a failing test but my own grep finding keys the checker said were not there. When a manual grep and a checker disagree, the checker is the thing under suspicion.
lessons.a_clean_working_tree_is_not_a_clean_publ: 2026-10-23 22:49 UTC: the credential checker reported CLEAN over 4166 tracked files and the tree really was scrubbed - and the pushed public master tip still served a Blotato key that returned HTTP 200 to an unauthenticated stranger fetching raw.githubusercontent.com. The checker scans the TREE; it cannot see a REMOTE. check-public-exposure.py scans every blob reachable from the pushed refs because a credential removed in the last commit is still in the last hundred commits. Rotation and redaction are two different jobs: rotate to kill the key, rewrite to remove the published copy, and do the rotation first.
lessons.a_damaged_index_looks_exactly_like_a_mas: 2026-10-27 16:26 UTC: the git index was replaced by a valid but EMPTY index (65 bytes, 0 entries) while HEAD tracked 15,921 files. git status showed all 15,921 as staged for deletion - and every one still existed on disk. One commit away from wiping the repo's tracking, and git status LOOKED like ground truth. The worktree was never touched; only the index was. Fix: git reset --mixed HEAD rebuilds the index from HEAD and touches no file in the worktree; --hard would have destroyed a worktree that was perfectly fine. The worktree is the truth; the index is a cache of it, and a cache can be corrupt while what it caches is fine. AND: on a damaged index, git add -A sweeps the phantom deletions into a commit - stage EXPLICIT PATHS and verify the staged set before committing.
lessons.a_dead_api_key_looks_exactly_like_an_emp: 2026-10-23: AGENTMAIL_API_KEY in .env returns HTTP 403. A sweep that ignores the status code reports 'no external mail' for a dead key. Always assert the sweep's own health (status + inbox count) before concluding anything from its result.
lessons.a_finished_tool_left_untracked_is_a_tool: 2026-10-23 23:19 UTC: the P0 remediation tool (history rewriter, 89 values, residual 0) was finished and verified but UNTRACKED, so it lived outside the repo and would not have survived a clean. Commit finished work that another session produced - after checking it for credential literals - rather than leaving the only path to a P0 unrecoverable.
lessons.a_green_verdict_needs_a_coverage_stateme: Every credential-audit blind spot in this incident was the same mistake in a different costume: a checker that only checks what it was told to check reports CLEAN and is wrong. (1) prefix-blind regex -> missed the Blotato key; (2) hardcoded file list -> missed the quarantine; (3) live-vs-unknown mismatch -> missed unprobeable keys; (4) prefix-only probing -> missed GoDaddy. The fix that generalises: a verdict must state what it did NOT check. The audit now prints a COVERAGE block (files read, files unreadable). Ask 'what did this NOT check?' before believing CLEAN.
lessons.a_guard_must_be_keyed_on_structure_not_p: 2026-10-23 23:45 UTC: the natural rule for 'this file was truncated' - the last line must end in terminal punctuation - gave 58 FALSE POSITIVES across 408 prose .md files in this repo (memory/2026-07-20.md ends '- HEARTBEAT_OK'). 'Ends without a trailing newline' was also wrong: HEAD:MEMORY.md and AGENTS.md end without one. A rule that fires on correct files teaches people to ignore it, which is worse than no rule. The guard is instead scoped to MEMORY.md and keyed on STRUCTURE (a committed ##-section must still exist), so rewording, reordering, adding and removing bullets inside a section all pass and only a whole section vanishing fails.
lessons.a_guard_that_blocks_a_build_job_is_still: 2026-10-24 00:15 UTC: the MEMORY.md shrink guard I shipped at 23:47 was correct and it worked - but it would have fired during 'Build Hour' (21:00 UTC) and turned a BUILD job red, losing that build's output, to protect a file the owner had been asked about but had not yet answered. A guard that only says 'no' is a veto, and a veto that fires on a scheduled job is a self-inflicted outage. The right response was to make the state correct - a MERGE that keeps every committed section and adds the session's new material - so the guard has nothing to block. The lesson is about the ORDER of fixes: restore the state first, then the guard is a safety net rather than a tripwire.
lessons.a_guard_that_fires_on_your_own_commit_is: 2026-10-23: the pre-commit credential guard blocked MY commit twice because my report script embedded live key values as literals. It was right both times. Match by PATTERN and take liveness from the untracked .env at runtime - never write a secret into the repo to describe a secret.
lessons.a_hand_rolled_probe_is_a_checker_with_no: 2026-10-26 16:14 UTC: there was no canonical latest-mail checker, so I hand-rolled one as a throwaway heredoc. It broke THREE ways inside one pass - the inbox list key is 'inboxes' not 'items', the handle is 'inbox_id' not 'address', the messages key is 'messages' not 'items' - and every failure printed the SAME reassuring thing: 'no new mail'. Miss the handle and `if not a: continue` skips every per-inbox fetch: zero fetches, zero errors, a confident 'newest: None'. A heredoc has no regression test, so nothing caught it. The fix was not patching the heredoc - it was making it a FILE with a test (ops/check-latest-mail.py + ops/test-check-latest-mail.py) that exits 2 rather than reporting 'no mail' when it cannot prove the answer. 🔑 A probe that produces a verdict needs to be a tested file, not a shell heredoc; and a zero is only a zero if you counted what you scanned.
lessons.a_knob_that_does_not_work_is_worse_than_: 2026-10-27: the pre-push guard documented GUARD_ENV_FILE, but load_env() took no path parameter so the guard always read /workspace/.env - the knob did NOTHING, and the test STILL PASSED because it was reading the real .env anyway. A knob is invisible precisely because it is inert. FIX: load_env(path=None) now accepts a path and the guard passes ENV_FILE; verified by pointing it at an empty file and observing zero credentials. GENERALISE: a test that passes is not evidence that the thing it exercises was used - a test must assert that turning the knob actually changed the outcome.
lessons.a_lesson_you_just_wrote_is_not_yet_a_hab: 2026-10-23: 40 minutes after documenting that limit=200 silently truncates a sweep, I wrote a new sweep with limit=50 and flagged 3 inboxes as truncated. The note is not a guard - put the assert (len(msgs) < limit) INSIDE the script.
lessons.a_negative_finding_is_only_as_strong_as_: 2026-10-23 (badge sweep): the AgentMail list endpoint populates 'text' for 0 of 2722 messages, the detail endpoint returns HTTP 400, and 'preview' exists for only 15% - so a 'no payment record' conclusion from a body scan is weaker than it looks. Enumerate every EXTERNAL SENDER as well: if no bank/organiser has ever written to us, that is independent evidence no payment happened. Say which fields you actually searched.
lessons.a_number_in_two_places_will_drift: 2026-10-23: the CIIE count lived in the recipients JSON and in the human-facing draft note. The JSON was corrected to 29; the note still said 26; every check passed. Validate the JSON's structure AND compare it to what a human will read. Drift rule 4b now does this.
lessons.a_probe_that_speaks_the_wrong_dialect_fa: 2026-10-24 08:33 UTC: the credential audit sent a bare Authorization header to AgentMail. 403 -> 'DEAD'. But DEAD is the class the redactor leaves in place, so a LIVE key was read as proof of death and left sitting in the active gateway log. The same bug had already been found once in the mail sweeps (404 route -> '0 messages'). A tool that cannot talk to the API will report the API's inaccessibility as the API's verdict.
lessons.a_push_blocker_can_be_two_problems_and_o: 2026-10-24 10:30 UTC: the GitHub push had been recorded as 'blocked by a dead PAT', which implies the fix is 'rotate the PAT'. Measuring it showed the blocker is TWO independent problems: (1) there is NO credential on the box at all (0-byte .git-credentials, no PAT in TOOLS.md/.env, no gh, no SSH key, credential fill returns nothing) and the published PAT is HTTP 401 'Bad credentials' - REVOKED, not misconfigured; (2) even with a working token, the push needs --force, because the local history was REWRITTEN and no longer shares a merge-base with origin/master. The second problem is the one that matters and it is invisible from 'the PAT is dead'. Worse, a rewrite-in-place makes '106 commits behind' LOOK like a collaborator pushed work we would clobber; it is our own discarded pre-rewrite lineage, and the remote has not moved since 2026-07-20. A recorded blocker that names only its most obvious cause sends the owner to fix the wrong thing.
lessons.a_test_fixture_that_holds_a_real_secret_: 2026-10-27: the guard test wrote a REAL live credential into a git object under /tmp. That path is in the tmp audit's FIXTURE_DIRS - the list that exists so SYNTHETIC tokens can be excluded - so a live key would have sat on disk UNFLAGGED if the test was killed mid-run. The exemption was doing exactly what it is designed to do (exclude synthetic material) and I had smuggled non-synthetic material underneath it. FIX: the test is hermetic (runtime-generated synthetic credential + synthetic env file); the real credential is proven WITHOUT writing it, by running the guard against the real repo's existing history where the literals already live in long-committed blobs. The fixture-ignore list must never exempt a path that can hold a real secret.
lessons.a_test_that_mirrors_the_code_proves_noth: 2026-10-23: my publish-path test re-implemented the pipeline inline, so it stayed green while the real scripts were mutated. Extract the shipping text into a callable function (build_platform_texts) and test THAT. Also: a fixture with only BALANCED '**' is masked by every safety net - the net exists for UNPAIRED markers, so the fixture must contain them.
lessons.a_test_that_runs_against_the_live_repo_i: 2026-10-27: the git index was emptied TWICE and no checker noticed. The cause was MY OWN test - ops/test-git-pre-push-guard.py called `git read-tree --empty` against the REAL index with no GIT_INDEX_FILE override (every other index call in that file used a scratch index correctly), and because the file is in ops/run-tests.sh, EVERY canonical suite run emptied the index. I repaired it twice and the second time went looking for an external culprit instead of asking: what runs every time the suite runs? The answer was in my own commit from that morning. THE DEEPER LESSON: a checker that only inspects the repo cannot catch a test that corrupts the repo - the worktree was never touched and every content check stayed green, so every instrument was looking at the wrong side of the fault. FIX: the test now builds its own throwaway repo and the guard takes GUARD_REPO / GUARD_ENV_FILE; the test also ASSERTS the real index is untouched.
lessons.a_tools_output_can_be_the_leak: stdout is captured into the gateway session log. A credential-HUNTING tool that prints what it finds has inverted its own purpose - ops/measure-cred-shapes.py printed every match verbatim, feeding the very log that held the live AgentMail keys. A tool's output is as dangerous as its input. Report candidates by shape (length + character classes + a short prefix), never by value.
lessons.a_truncated_reference_is_not_a_secret: research/2026-08-10.md:62 holds a PREFIX of the live BLOTATO_API_KEY - a truncated reference, not a usable credential. Distinguish 'matches a live credential exactly' from 'is a prefix of one' before calling a tracked value an exposure.
lessons.a_verifier_that_only_rechecks_what_it_ac: 2026-10-24 08:33 UTC: three false greens in one credential toolchain, all the same shape. (1) The audit probed AgentMail with a bare Authorization header; the API answers 403 to that and 200 to 'Authorization: Bearer <key>', so every LIVE AgentMail key read as DEAD - and DEAD is the one class the redactor leaves in place. (2) The redactor early-returned when a scan found no LIVE credential, so a file holding only UNKNOWN literals was skipped. (3) The redactor's verify step re-checked ONLY the LIVE class, so it printed 'no credential literal remains' over a file full of UNKNOWN ones. The pattern across all of them: each tool reported on a narrower slice of the world than it was responsible for, and so called a partial success a clean one. A verifier that only re-checks the class it just acted on cannot see the class it did not act on.
lessons.check_which_account_before_believing_a_c: 2026-10-23: the main AgentMail key 404s the CIIE inbox, so a sweep with it reported 0 sends and a 'MISMATCH - revise before sending' verdict that was purely a credential artefact. Also limit=200 silently truncated a 392-message inbox, excluding the entire window under investigation. Assert len(msgs) < limit.
lessons.checker_scripts_must_verify_their_own_cr: 12 scripts shipped literal '${...}' key placeholders as the credential value -> HTTP 403 -> printed '0 messages', identical to 'nothing there'. Fixed in b47f27df via scripts/agentmail_keys.py (live_agentmail_keys() PROBES each key and refuses to report a zero if none is live; assert_not_truncated fails loud when count == limit). Negative-tested by ops/test-key-resolution.py. Also: verify-ciii-breach-count.py swept only the MAIN key, so the CIIE inbox (a different AgentMail account) read as 0/12 and printed a false MISMATCH on the correction note; the 29/12 figures were correct. Re-verified 12/12 recipients, 29 emails. This is the FOURTH confident zero from the same shape (404 route, items-vs-posts key, limit=6 window, wrong ACCOUNT).
lessons.concurrent_sessions: 2026-10-22: a parallel cron session (agent:main:cron:5ffb50d9-...) committed 3 changes mid-pass and correctly corrected an error in my Discord post. Verify the other agent's claim against RAW data, and verify your own before defending it. Also: never write a commit hash before the commit exists - read it back from git log.
lessons.correct_the_facts_before_asking_for_appr: 2026-10-23: the correction draft said 'Send from: sales@studex-group.com (the inbox they were contacted from)'. They were contacted from project-2571-studex-agent-2077@agentmail.to - a different AgentMail account. Asking Tumelo to approve a send with a wrong fact in it gets a wrong answer.
lessons.count_git_records_with_dash_z_not_split: 2026-10-27: a new checker counted tracked files with .split() on git's default output and reported 16,035 for a repo that tracks 15,922. Git QUOTES paths containing spaces or non-ASCII, so one path becomes three tokens. Use `-z` (NUL-separated, unquoted) and count records. A wrong number in the output meant to establish trust is worse than no output.
lessons.cron_edit_cron_resets_the_timezone: 2026-10-23: `openclaw cron edit <id> --cron <expr>` RESETS tz to UTC unless --tz is passed with it. Editing a SAST job's hour silently moved it 2h LATE. Always pass --cron AND --tz, and verify by reading nextRunAtMs back from jobs.json - the expr alone cannot tell you when a job fires.
lessons.do_not_run_the_suite_and_the_heartbeat_p: 2026-10-27: running ops/run-tests.sh and ops/run-heartbeat-checks.py at the same time produced FALSE failures in ops/test-credential-resolution.py and ops/test-tmp-shape-surface-audit.py - both PASSED standalone and both passed in the sequential run. Both mutate /tmp fixtures. Run them SEQUENTIALLY; a red suite under concurrency is not a regression, and chasing it wastes the budget. (A concurrent session hit the same thing at 16:03 UTC.)
lessons.enumerate_every_sender_not_the_one_you_r: 2026-10-22: we believed dist/cli.js sent nothing. It sent 3 emails to named leads in data/state.json - addresses absent from prospects.json. Building the correction list from the file we remembered would have skipped a third of the recipients. Enumerate every engine AND every state file, and verify the recipient list against what was actually sent, not against the list we kept.
lessons.fewer_headings_is_not_the_same_memory: 2026-10-23 23:19 UTC: a concurrent session rewrote MEMORY.md mid-flight - 23 headings to 9, ending mid-sentence. Measured against HEAD, the drop was not cosmetic: the CIIE badge, the Blotato roster + Meta-token blocker, the Zatsepilov lead, the GitHub PAT blocker and the Saudi RFQ all lost their entries. 'Fewer headings' is not 'the same memory' - a trimmed long-term file that drops every open P0 is a SHORTER memory a future session cannot act from. And a truncation is not a completion: a file ending mid-sentence is an in-flight write, so the honest read of 'less' is work in progress, not cleanup. Did not edit it (it was actively being written); flagged it to the owner instead.
lessons.measure_the_disk_before_guessing_which_p: 2026-10-23 22:49 UTC: the overlay was at 83%/5.0G free and a checker had already died with 'No space left on device'. The cause was /root/.npm at 11G - a cache - which no amount of checking /workspace would have surfaced. The previous pass had already reclaimed 505M from a disposable clone and left the 11G untouched. The biggest thing was not the thing that looked biggest. And never delete a concurrent session's worktree: /tmp/studex-scrub was live.
lessons.prove_the_checker_fires: 2026-10-22: the correction-rule test fixture was malformed (triple backticks nested inside the heredoc), which made a passing case look like a failing one and briefly sent me chasing a bug that wasn't in the checker. Build fixtures programmatically, not inside a shell heredoc, and re-verify with a control case before concluding anything.
lessons.removing_a_false_claim_from_one_page_is_: 2026-10-23: 'Rainforest Alliance certified' was removed from the STATIC China page on 2026-10-21 and survived on the React China page, live, for a day. A claim removed from one surface must be searched for on every surface - especially any surface the checker cannot see.
lessons.scan_all_fenced_blocks: 2026-10-22: draft_body() took only the FIRST fenced block. A draft may fence both the email body and a send command (kfschof-reply.md does). Taking only the first means the body can be silently skipped - an unchecked body is worse than a false positive. Now returns ALL blocks.
lessons.scrubbing_the_tree_is_not_the_same_as_re: 2026-10-23: the credential scrubber skipped log/history directories, but those are TRACKED in a public repo, so live keys stay published - and stay in git history no matter what you edit. For a public repo the complete fix is ROTATE then rewrite history. Skipping a path is not a security control.
lessons.something_that_looks_like_a_control_and_: 2026-10-27, three instances in one afternoon, all mine: the EMPTY knob (GUARD_ENV_FILE), the guard installed at a path git ignores (core.hooksPath=.githooks), and the checker that validated that same wrong path. Each had a docstring or a diff line making it look finished. PROSE AND CONFIGURATION ARE NOT EVIDENCE - only an assertion that the thing is load-bearing is. A checker that validates a path nothing reads always passes.
lessons.the_fourth_false_green_a_detector_that_o: 2026-10-24 09:25 UTC: four false greens in one credential toolchain, all the same shape - each tool reported on a narrower slice of the world than it was responsible for, and so called a partial success a clean one. The fourth: ops/check-scanner-log-exposure.py, whose entire job is catching a credential printed into the gateway log, found candidates only by matching ONE tool's line format. The surface audit measured 18 live/unknown literals in that log; this checker reported zero, because the other tools printed in formats it did not recognise. A leak a detector cannot SEE is reported as a leak that did not happen - which is worse than having no detector, because the presence of the detector suppresses the search. The fix pattern that generalises: two tools answering the same question must share ONE definition of the answer (loaded by path, not re-implemented), and the verdict must be carried by the EXIT CODE so a found-but-not-failing leak cannot be forgotten.
lessons.unverified_is_not_safe: 2026-10-23 22:49 UTC: check-public-exposure.py exits 1 with UNVERIFIED when it cannot establish liveness. 'We could not prove it works' is not 'it is safe'. A 400 or 404 is a request-shape error, never proof of death. Probing the Meta page tokens myself showed both expired 27-Jun-2026 - so an UNDETERMINED verdict is a coverage limit, not a live exposure. Do not escalate an undetermined finding as if it were a live breach, and do not let it be downgraded as if it were safe.

fourth_pass_2026_10_24_08_33_utc.lesson: THREE false greens in one toolchain, all the same shape: each tool reported on a narrower slice of the world than it was responsible for, and so called a partial success a clean one. The audit knew about UNKNOWN; the redactor did not. The audit knew about LIVE; the redactor's verify did not. The probe spoke the wrong dialect and so saw DEAD. A green verdict is only as wide as the scan behind it - and a verifier that only re-checks the class it just acted on cannot see the class it did not act on.
